items.title: "Shop all" has aria-current="page" on the catalog page
covers: Expected: on the catalog page the header's Shop all link has aria-current="page"
items.reason: This is the bug itself: on the catalog the link is styled as current but a screen reader is not told so. It needs the rendered page in a browser, so it is an e2e case; no cheaper layer renders the Blazor header with the endpoint metadata that decides the current page.

items.title: "Shop all" keeps its text, destination and is-current look on the catalog page
covers: Expected: its text, destination and look are unchanged (catalog page)
items.reason: The fix must add only the attribute; the story requires the link's text, destination and look to stay as they were. A regression here (renamed link, broken href, lost highlight) would be visible to every shopper, so it is checked separately from the attribute case. e2e because only the rendered page shows the final markup.

items.title: "Shop all" has no aria-current on a product page
covers: Expected: on a product page the link has no aria-current
items.reason: The story requires the attribute to be absent (not `false`, not empty) on non-catalog pages; announcing "current page" on a product page would be a new accessibility bug. Step 3 of the reproduction names the product page explicitly. e2e because the header is rendered per route on the server.

items.title: "Shop all" has no aria-current on the shopping bag
covers: Expected: on the shopping bag the link has no aria-current
items.reason: The shopping bag is one of the three non-catalog pages the story names. It is a different page component from the product page and sits behind sign-in, so it gets its own case to prove the attribute depends on the catalog page only, not on some other page property.

items.title: "Shop all" has no aria-current on My orders
covers: Expected: on My orders the link has no aria-current
items.reason: My orders is the third non-catalog page the story names. It is a separate authenticated page component; a case here guards against the attribute being tied to anything but the catalog page.

items.title: "Shop all" keeps its text and destination and has no is-current look on a product page
covers: Expected: its text, destination and look are unchanged (other pages)
items.reason: "Text, destination and look unchanged" applies on every page. On non-catalog pages the link must still lead to the catalog and must not gain the current-page highlight. Clicking it proves the destination end to end rather than only reading the `href`.

items.title: aria-current follows in-app navigation from the catalog to a product and back
covers: Steps to Reproduce 1-3 as a user navigates
Expected: aria-current="page" on the catalog only
items.reason: The reproduction steps move from the catalog to a product page. The WebApp uses Blazor enhanced navigation, which patches the existing DOM instead of reloading it, so a stale `aria-current="page"` could survive on the product page (or fail to come back) even when direct loads (TC-01, TC-03) are right. Only a browser driving real clicks exercises this.
